SECOND NEAR-MISS ON MY OWN SIDE, printed because hiding it would make this record worth less -- and it is the very defect this PR is about. To run mutation probe P3 I copied the reviewed worktree with `cp -r`. A git worktree's `.git` is a FILE pointing back into the main repository's .git/worktrees/<name>, so the copy was NOT independent: P3's deliberately bad-identity commit (`Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`, sha cbbffe9) was written onto the branch I was about to push from. I caught it with `git status` / `git log` before staging anything, and reset hard back to c07c498d0aa5a54561224e4e5ae60a413265f78f (verified: HEAD == the PR head, working tree clean apart from this untracked record). Nothing was pushed. Had I not looked, I would have pushed to this PR's branch the exact bad-commit-identity defect that forced the re-cuts of #38, #49, #52, #55 and #65 -- and reviewer A did precisely that to #49, per HANDOFF.md item 3. Two lessons worth leaving here: probe in a directory that is not a copy of a worktree, and a reviewer's own record-only commit is a real opportunity to break the branch it is meant to unblock.
